title: Willie Humphrey, Educational Gateways, and Clyde Kerr Sr. as teachers
summary: He identifies Willie Humphrey as his clarinet teacher, won through a Sunday radio show scholarship at about age 12-13, and praises Clyde Kerr Sr. as a major teacher.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the first horn: clarinet and saxophone beginnings

blocks.x: Okay. Was that Clyde Kerr Sr. who said that to you? Who was your teacher who said that you came?

Willie Humphrey, who's still alive and I think in his 80s now one of the great clarinet players. He and his brother Percy play down at Preservation Hall but Willie Humphrey I met through a scholarship I used to play on the radio every Sunday afternoon when I was in junior high school on a Peter Champ Clark show that was called Stars of Tomorrow and at that time my influences were Earl Bostic and Louis Jordan and I liked Sam Butera during that time and I remember him making a comment one time when I was playing saying who knows maybe he'll be another Charlie Parker and I was about 12, 13 years old and I said Charlie Parker, who's that? because I wasn't quite I didn't become aware of Bird until like a little later on like just as I was about to enter high school and I really knew what he meant and from that radio show I won a scholarship to Educational Gateways and Willie Humphrey happened to be my clarinet teacher but of Clyde Kerr Sr. there's not enough that can be said about him I think maybe a good 70, 75% of all of the good musicians that you hear playing now at some point came through him the man made a he consecrated his life to teaching and passing on and writing music now that's an institution that really needs some exploration because he and Alvin Batiste I often say are probably the two most profound music teachers that I've ever had not only because of what they gave me musically but they gave so much of them stuff
